subject: POC: async sockets & concurrency qualification / credit request
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lchen@aegishealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aegishealth.com
Date: 2026-10-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: latency & concurrency needs for Aegis POC

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo today — it was helpful to see the streaming controls and fallbacks. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the performance targets and concurrency shape from our side so you can propose a quota/rate path we can review with procurement.

Summary of our current understanding and asks:
- Latency targets: 100ms p95 for single-turn text generation; streaming ingest-to-first-token target ~200ms median.
- Expected parallel requests: steady-state 120 concurrent requests, spike to 450 for 30s during daytime peak.
- Connection pooling: we keep persistent websockets from 75 app servers; estimate ~600 concurrent TCP sockets at peak.
- Streaming sessions: ~80 long-lived streaming sessions concurrently (chat + audio transcription).
- Throughput: average token generation ~12k tokens/minute; peak bursts up to 40k tokens/minute.

Immediate asks:
1) Can Redwood support these p95 latency targets with a hosted pilot or do we recommend Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency?
2) What connection/concurrency limits would you propose for a 30-day pilot and for production if we commit to a Reserved (Dedicated) pool?
3) Any temporary credits you can offer for the pilot and an estimated monthly ratecard with the concurrency tiers you propose.

I've attached the usage worksheet we filled out during the call. Procurement looped in on cc — they'll want a short written proposal and any SOC / compliance links.

Thanks,
Lydia Chen
Director of AI Platforms
Aegis Health

Attachment: aegis-request-sheet.xlsx (1 sheet)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lchen@aegishealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency & concurrency needs for Aegis POC

Lydia — thanks for the clear recap and the worksheet, that helps a lot. A few quick answers and the proposed next steps.

Quick answers:
- Pilot recommendation: We can validate the latency targets on our Hosted API with an optimized model variant and intelligent routing, but to guarantee 100ms p95 at the scale you describe we generally recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) — especially given the burst to 450 concurrent requests and sustained socket counts.
- Pilot concurrency proposal (temporary): we can open a 30-day pilot with soft quota of 200 concurrent requests and a burst allowance to 500 for short windows (30s–2m) to match your peak pattern. For sockets, we'll mirror that with 700 allowed connections during the pilot.
- Production (Reserved): For a committed Dedicated pool we propose capacity sizing at 400 steady concurrent requests with a 1.5x burst buffer; connection ceiling 900 sockets.
- Credits: We can offer $25k in platform credit for pilot validation contingent on using our standard pilot SOW.

Next steps I propose:
1) Neha (cc) will send a short technical questionnaire describing request/response sizes and expected token distribution so we can tune kernel/quantization choices.
2) I'll circulate an initial ratecard (attached) with 3 tiers: Pilot, Committed Dedicated, Enterprise SLA.
3) Procurement: we can provide SOC2 link and a short SOW for the pilot.

I'll put the ratecard and a sample connection profile on this thread. If that looks ok to procurement, Marissa can follow up with contracting.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the numbers.

— Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-initial-ratecard-v1.pdf (3 pages)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lchen@aegishealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: latency & concurrency needs for Aegis POC

Lydia — quick technical follow-up from the SE side. Appreciate the worksheet. Two clarifying asks so we can produce a tighter quota proposal:

1) Request distribution: is your 120 steady concurrent an even distribution of short requests (~1–2s) or are these long streaming sessions? You mentioned chat + transcription; can you split expected concurrent sessions by type (short-gen vs. streaming) and median token/second for each?

2) Failure tolerance: do you require hard SLAs during the pilot (we can set soft quotas) or are occasional transient throttles acceptable while we validate scaling?

What we can do technically during the pilot:
- Reserve a dedicated fraction of a GPU pool to validate p95 numbers with your workload profile.
- Enable prefix/KV caching and tuning for chat sessions to cut token costs and reduce latency for repeated contexts.
- Provision a temporary connection pool ceiling (attached sample profile) we can increase during controlled bursts.

I'll attach a small CSV with a sample connection profile and a template for the request breakdown — if you fill that and return it, we'll generate a formal quota/ratecard proposal within 48 hours.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: conn-profile-sample.csv (1 file)

Thanks Diego and Neha — this is helpful. Procurement has reviewed the worksheet and gave a green light to proceed with a pilot, subject to the pilot SOW and SOC2 link. A couple of follow-ups:

- Procurement asks for a written pilot SOW and the formal ratecard you mentioned. Can Marissa or Diego please send that and confirm the $25k pilot credit in writing?
- For the technical questionnaire: we will return the filled-in request profile by EOD Friday.
- Can you confirm whether the pilot quota of 200 concurrent requests + burst to 500 will require us to use the Hosted API or if Redwood will provision a short-lived Dedicated slice? Procurement prefers a short-lived Dedicated slice if it reduces risk of throttles during evaluation.

If you can send the SOW and the initial ratecard and SOC link this week, we can get PR approved and start the pilot next week.

Lydia
Director of AI Platforms, Aegis Health
